answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with provenance-clustered, time-locked stake. Each identity locks a refundable bond that vests like a glacier — voting weight accrues only across a long horizon, so a mint-attack buys no instant power. The ledger traces each bond's funding history: the ocean of transactions betrays the attacker, since identities funded from the same source are clustered and share one vote. A thousand minted accounts win nothing beyond the first; real influence demands independent backers or capital frozen long enough to hurt.
